problem: Models like CSCG learn cognitive maps of aliased environments only after long random or hard-coded exploration and cannot extrapolate to unseen areas. They need many steps to learn structure, unlike animals that learn in one or a few visits.
motivation: Animals navigate ambiguous, aliased environments by combining memory, imagination and proprioception, and learn layouts very quickly. An agent that imagines the outcomes of actions and expands its map with placeholder states can be drawn to unexplored places and learn structure with little data and no prior knowledge of map size or observation type.
key_idea: Combine a growing topological map with internal position (proprioception) in an active-inference POMDP, and expand the map with imagined, observation-less states so that expected free energy (information gain) drives exploration.
insight: Imagined states with uniform observation likelihood are highly uncertain, so information gain pulls the agent toward unexplored areas. This makes exploration close to the oracle step count, while CSCG revisits known rooms. CSCG with position as an observation, a random policy, or Viterbi navigation does not close the gap. The paper argues this shows the benefit of map extension over unvisited areas. Imagined transitions use a lower learning rate than experienced ones, so the agent confirms its priors instead of over-trusting them.
method: Hierarchical abstraction: lower layers turn observations into one colour per room and handle blocked paths (walls keep the pose static, doors lead to a new state); the AIF POMDP works at the highest level.

POMDP with pose: hidden states s_t (room) and position p_t are inferred jointly from the previous state, pose and action, using variational inference. Proprioception disambiguates aliased observations, and a confidence threshold handles kidnapping/relocalisation.

Parameter learning with dynamic growth: A_o, A_p and B_s are learned by free-energy minimisation and their state dimensions grow (similar to Bayesian model reduction). B_p is an incremental pose-transition process with no learned parameters.

Imagined map expansion: one-step policy outcomes are predicted in all unobstructed directions, and new states with uniform observation likelihood are added. Imagined transitions get a lower learning rate than experienced ones.
Policy selection: policies are chosen by softmax(-γG) over expected free energy, with no preference (utility) term, so behaviour is driven by information gain alone.
CSCG baselines: CSCG with a Viterbi path estimator (updated every 5 steps), with the paper's state estimation, with random policy, and 'CSCG pose ob' where position is added as an observation.

setting.backbone: Active inference POMDP with online Bayesian parameter learning (A_o, A_p, B_s) and a dynamically growing topological graph; no neural network
setting.training_data: none; online learning within a single exploration episode per environment
setting.observation: Single discrete floor colour per room (aliased), plus internal proprioception/pose from actions
setting.privileged: none for the agent; ground-truth transition matrix used only to judge exploration completion (60% certainty threshold)

numbers_note: Results are only given in figures (average steps on a log scale, Fig. 3a/3b) and not in tables, so no numeric values are extractable. The benchmark is a custom MiniGrid room-exploration task.
results: In 3x3 and 4x4 room grids, T-maze and donut mazes, with and without aliasing, the agent learns the topology in far fewer steps than CSCG variants. Its room-discovery steps closely match the oracle. CSCG occasionally fails within the step budget, while the proposed agent always succeeds. Giving CSCG the pose reduces its training by about 100 steps in aliased square environments and about 200 in T-mazes, but it still lags behind.
limitations: Evaluated only in small, discrete, toy grid-room environments with single-colour room observations and hierarchical abstraction assumed; no standard navigation benchmark and no real robot.

Only one-step lookahead for imagining new states; no goal-directed navigation with preferences was tested; exploration success threshold (60%) is arbitrary; results are figures only, with at least 10 runs per environment.
builds_on: Hierarchical spatial AIF (de Tinguy et al. 2024)
